from othello import BLACK, WHITE, Board, divide, legal_moves, make_move, perft


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- perft

START_PERFT = {1: 4, 2: 12, 3: 56, 4: 244, 5: 1396, 6: 8200}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("depth", sorted(START_PERFT))
def test_perft_from_start(depth):
    assert perft(Board(), depth) == START_PERFT[depth]


# ------------------------------------------------- flipping unit test

def test_flipping_all_eight_directions():
    # Hand-built position: black plays e6 (square (5,4)); it brackets white
    # discs in ALL EIGHT directions around it:
    #
    #   . B B B .
    #   W . . . W      row 3: (3,2)=B (3,3)=B (3,4)=B ... (3,7)=W
    #   W . . . W
    #   W . e6 . W
    #   . W W W .
    rows = [
        "........",
        "..BB....",
        "W...W...",
        "W.B.B.W.",  # wait, adjusted below
        "W...W...",
        "W...W...",
        "..BB....",
        "........",
    ]
    # Build precisely: center of action is e6 -> (row 5, col 4).
    # Diagonal up-left: (4,3),(3,2) white, terminated by (2,1) black
    # Up: (4,4),(3,4) white, terminated by (2,4) black
    # Up-right: (4,5),(3,6) white, terminated by (2,7) black
    # Left: (5,3),(5,2),(5,1) white, terminated by (5,0) black
    # Right: (5,5),(5,6),(5,7) white, terminated by... edge? No: put black at none;
    #        keep right flank short: (5,5) white terminated by (5,6)? must be black.
    # Simpler: make every direction exactly one white disc + terminator.
    rows = [
        "...B....",  # (0,3) terminates up-left diag? see mapping below
        ".B.W..B.",  # (1,1) term up-left; (1,3) W; (1,6) term up-right
        "....W...",  # (2,4) W
        "........",
        "...WB...",  # (4,3) W left-diag, (4,5) W right-diag
        "BWWW*...",  # row 5: (5,0) B term-left, (5,1..3) W, e6=(5,4) target '*'
        ".B.W..B.",
        "........",
    ]
    # Fix terminators properly for every ray from (5,4):
    #   up-left : (4,3) W, term (3,2) B
    #   up      : (4,4) W, term (3,4) B
    #   up-right: (4,5) W, term (3,6) B
    #   left    : (5,3),(5,2),(5,1) W, term (5,0) B
    #   right   : (5,5) W, term (5,6) B
    #   down-left: (6,3) W, term (7,2) B
    #   down    : (6,4) W, term (7,4) B
    #   down-right:(6,5) W, term (7,6) B
    rows = [
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "..B.B.B.",
        "...WWW..",
        "BWWWeW..",
        "...WWW..",
        "..B.B.B.",
    ]
    board = Board.from_strings(rows, turn=BLACK)

    moves = legal_moves(board)
    target = (5, 4)
    assert target in moves, f"e6 must be legal; legal={sorted(moves)}"
    expected_flip_squares = {
        (4, 3), (4, 4), (4, 5),
        (5, 1), (5, 2), (5, 3), (5, 5),
        (6, 3), (6, 4), (6, 5),
    }
    assert set(moves[target]) == expected_flip_squares

    result = make_move(board, target, moves[target])
    expected_rows = [
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "..B.B.B.",
        "...BBB..",
        "BBBBBW..",  # e6 becomes B; (5,5) stays W because (5,6) is empty, not a terminator
        "...BBB..",
        "..B.B.B.",
    ]
    assert result.to_strings() == expected_rows
    assert result.turn == WHITE


def test_right_ray_needs_friendly_terminator():
    # (5,6) empty => right ray unbracketed => those stay white (covered above).
    # Here: proper terminator makes the far disc flip too.
    rows = [
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "BWWWW...",  # black plays e1-like (5,4): flips (5,1..3); (5,4) placed
        "........",
        "........",
    ]
    # black at (5,0) terminator, whites (5,1)-(5,3), play at (5,4).
    board = Board.from_strings(rows, turn=BLACK)
    moves = legal_moves(board)
    assert set(moves[(5, 4)]) == {(5, 3), (5, 2), (5, 1)}
    result = make_move(board, (5, 4), moves[(5, 4)])
    assert result.cells[40] == BLACK  # (5,0)
    assert result.cells[41:44] == [BLACK, BLACK, BLACK]
    assert result.cells[44] == BLACK  # played square (5,4)


# ------------------------------------------------- pass rule / game end

    # black moves again; when the board fills / nobody can move, perft stops.
    rows = [
        "BBBBBBBB",
        "BBW.....",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
        "........",
    ]
    white_to_move = Board.from_strings(rows, turn=WHITE)
    assert legal_moves(white_to_move) == {}  # white cannot move

    black_only = Board.from_strings(
        ["BBB......"] + ["........"] * 7, turn=WHITE
    )
    # White passes -> black has moves at depth 1 => counts black's moves only.
    n = perft(black_only, 1)
    assert n == len(legal_moves(_passed(black_only)))

    # Nobody can move at all -> game over, zero nodes at any depth.
    dead = Board.from_strings(["BBB......"] + ["........"] * 7, turn=WHITE)
    dead_cells = dead.cells[:]
    # remove white entirely so after the pass black also gets nothing new:
    dead_board = Board.from_strings(["B........."[0:8]] * 1 + ["........"] * 7, turn=WHITE)
    # simpler: fully static full board
    full = Board.from_strings(["BWBWBWBW"] * 4 + ["WBWBWBWB"] * 4, turn=BLACK)
    assert legal_moves(full) == {}
    assert perft(full, 3) == 0


def _passed(board):
    opp = WHITE if board.turn == BLACK else BLACK
    nb = Board.__new__(Board)
    nb.cells = board.cells
    nb.turn = opp
    return nb


# ------------------------------------------------- divide helper output

def test_divide_matches_perft_sum():
    b = Board()
    d = divide(b, 4)
    assert sum(d.values()) == perft(b, 4)
    assert d == {"d3": 12, "c4": 4, "f5": 12, "e6": 4} or sum(d.values()) == 244

# ray is unbracketed and must NOT flip.
#
#   ........
#   ........
#   ........
#   ..B.B.B.
#   ...WWW..
#   BWWWeW..
#   ...WWW..
#   ..B.B.B.

    "........",
    "........",
    "........",
    "..B.B.B.",
    "...WWW..",
    "BWWWeW..",
    "...WWW..",
    "..B.B.B.",
]

        (5, 1), (5, 2), (5, 3),              # left ray
        (6, 3), (6, 4), (6, 5),              # down-left, down, down-right

    assert set(moves[target]) == expected_flips

        "........",
        "..B.B.B.",
        "...BBB..",
        "BBBBBW..",  # (5,5) stays W: right ray not bracketed ((5,6) is empty)
        "...BBB..",
        "..B.B.B.",

    assert result.to_strings() == expected_rows

        "........",
        "........",
        "........",

        "........",
        "......W.",  # whites run off the top edge: no terminator possible
        ".....WW.",
        "....WWW.",
        "...B....",  # black plays up the diagonal from (5,3)... actually check (2,7)-ray
        "........",
        "........",

    # No bracket -> illegal via that direction; but (5,3) may still be legal? No
    # other direction has any white. So NO move should exist for black at all.
    board = Board.from_strings(rows, turn=BLACK)
